papers.summary: Two-page Snowmass 2022 white paper (12 authors) listing the group's research directions. It restates C1's identification as 'dark matter should be viewed as a dual SM', the dual being 'the dual spacetime' of a general non-commutative string theory, credited to Minic 2020 and Berglund–Hübsch–Minic 2021; it does not say the dual is the momentum side. The dark-matter phenomenology it envisages is the observed galactic and cluster scaling correlations among dark matter, dark energy and visible matter, as an open aim; no coupling, detection prediction, dynamics or monopoles. Dark energy is the dual spacetime's geometry and dynamical; no w. 'Vacuum selection' is selection among string vacua (the origin of the SM's content) by a biophysics-inspired mechanism, not selection of a polarization.

answers.answer: Four of the nine papers restate the identification, always credited to Minic 2020 (arXiv:2003.00318) and Berglund–Hübsch–Minic, LHEP 2021 (arXiv:2010.15610), and always as a proposal. (1) The Snowmass paper 2202.05104 says 'dark matter should be viewed as a dual SM'. It states this as the group's approach and says it 'has been recently proposed [29, 30]'. (2) 2202.06890 and Addazi et al. §2.2.2.5 say each observed field's 'dual' 'could be associated with dark matter', a proposal. (3) Addazi §2.3.4 lists 'their “duals”, associated with dark matter degrees of freedom' as an observable hallmark. Its §2.2.2.3 calls 'dual matter and dual gravity sectors' a generic prediction of modular spacetime but does not name dark matter in that sentence. (4) 2011.08852 §6 says the dual part of the matter sector 'can be naturally related to the dark matter sector that is sensitive to dark energy', a proposal citing the modified-dark-matter papers. Five papers do not state it. 2202.05266 is agnostic about the theory. In 2503.20854 dark matter is part of the matter Lagrangian 'put in by hand'. 2212.00901 and 2303.17495 have no dark sector. 2312.00409 has only a bullet on the metaparticle and Born reciprocity. None of the nine says the dual is the momentum side; each describes it as 'the dual spacetime' of a non-commutative, T-duality covariant string theory.
evidence: 2202.05104, paragraph 'Constraints on the nature of dark matter'

answers.question: Q2
answers.answer: These papers use x̃ in two senses. (a) In the dark-energy papers (2011.08852 §2; 2503.20854 §1 and App. B), x̃ is the string's left-minus-right coordinate in a doubled target space X^A = (x/λ, x̃/λ). The scale is λ = √α′, 'the string length scale' ('such as the Planck scale'). The commutators are [x̂^a, x̃̂_b] = 2πiλ²δ^a_b and [x, x] = [x̃, x̃] = 0 (2011.08852 eq. 8; 2503.20854 eq. 101); 2503.20854 §1–§2 write iλ², a factor 2π apart. They call the doubled space phase space ('works in phase space', 'doubled “phase-space” operators') and x̃-space 'canonically conjugate', because it does not commute with x. The metaparticle has separate momenta p and dual momenta p̃ with p p̃ = μ (2503.20854 §3.4): the space is doubled, and its scale is λ², not ℏ. No [x, p] or [x̃, p̃] is given in the nine papers. (b) In the vacuum-energy papers (2212.00901 eqs. 10–11; 2303.17495 eq. 5), (x, x̃) are the coordinates of a modular cell of ordinary phase space: q = λx, p = εx̃, with λε = 2πℏ. There x̃ is momentum at ℏ, the program's sense, but these papers have no dark sector. The Snowmass paper and Addazi et al. give no definition beyond 'dual spacetime' and 'T-duality covariant and intrinsically non-commutative'. This agrees with the record: the dark-sector model doubles phase space at the string scale where the program polarizes one phase space (#11 P2′, P4).

answers.question: Q3
answers.answer: The Snowmass paper calls the dark sector a whole dual Standard Model ('a dual SM'). 2202.06890 and Addazi §2.2.2.5 give one dual per observed quantum field. Addazi §2.2.2.3 speaks of 'dual matter and dual gravity sectors', and 2011.08852 §6 of 'the dual part of the matter sector'. Addazi and 2202.06890 also list axion-like backgrounds from non-commutativity. None of the nine discusses a dual photon, dual charges or a gauge structure of the dual sector.
evidence: 2202.05104, 'Constraints on the nature of dark matter'

answers.question: Q4
answers.answer: None of the nine papers writes a coupling term, a strength or a correlation function between the dual and the visible sector, and 'entangled' never appears for the dark sector. 'Correlated' appears in two papers. The Snowmass paper names 'intriguing correlations between dark matter, dark energy, and visible matter on the galactic, and galaxy cluster scales [8, 9]', observed correlations it aims to explain ('we would like to understand whether'). 2202.06890 has '(Dark matter, dark energy and visible matter are naturally correlated in this description [45, 46].)', with refs [45, 46] the modified-dark-matter papers (Ho–Minic–Ng 2010; Edmonds et al. 2017). The second of these places the correlation 'in correlations between dark matter and baryonic matter in galaxy rotation curves', through a critical acceleration related to Λ (its abstract, read via lit.py show). Addazi et al. cite the same two papers for 'consistent with observations'. 2011.08852 ties the dual matter sector to 'the dark matter sector that is sensitive to dark energy', also modified dark matter. On limits, 2011.08852 and 2503.20854 say that to zeroth (2503: first) order in λ, x and x̃ commute and the action separates into R(x) + R̃(x̃). The dual geometry then reaches ours only through G_N and Λ, and x–x̃ mixing arises at higher order in λ. 2503.20854's argument that Λ changes with our scale factor rests on the non-commutativity. A larger dual space means weaker gravity (1/G_N ∼ dual volume). My reading: in these nine papers 'correlated' names the observed MOND-like scaling of halos with baryons and Λ, not a stated coupling beyond gravity. Whether the school's dual sector couples beyond gravity must be judged from Minic 2020 and Berglund–Hübsch–Minic 2021 and 2023, which are not among my papers. #11 P4 (strict) and §13 row 7 require gravity alone.
evidence: 2202.05104, 'Constraints on the nature of dark matter'
1709.04388, abstract (cited source, read via lit.py show)

answers.question: Q5
answers.answer: None of the nine papers makes a direct-detection or collider prediction for the dual sector, and none discusses the null results or a permanent null. The phenomenology they name is of three kinds. (1) Galactic and cluster scaling relations, as an aim (Snowmass; its ref [31] is Dai and Lu 2017 on MOND-like behaviour in ΛCDM simulations). (2) Modified-dark-matter correlations with a critical acceleration related to Λ, via the references of 2202.06890 and Addazi et al. (3) For observed quanta, 'the most specific prediction': an IR-deformed metaparticle dispersion relation E_p² + μ²/E_p² = p² + m², with μ of order 10⁻² eV² for neutrinos (2202.06890). One cited source bears on the null results: the modified-dark-matter review 1709.04388 (abstract only) says non-local aspects of its quanta 'may explain why, so far, dark matter detection experiments have failed to detect dark matter particles'. That is conditional, and it is about modified-dark-matter quanta, which 2011.08852 links to the dual sector. Compare #11 §13 row 7 ('Permanent null').
evidence: 2202.05104, 'Constraints on the nature of dark matter'

answers.question: Q6
answers.answer: Newton's constant is set by the dual space's volume and the cosmological constant by its curvature: 1/G_N ∼ ∫√(−g̃) and Λ/G_N ∼ ∫√(−g̃) R̃ (2011.08852 eqs. 11–12; 2503.20854 eqs. 4–5 and 104–105). In their words, 'the weakness of gravity is determined by the size of the canonically conjugate dual x̃-space'. The dual spacetime has its own metric g̃(x̃). 2503.20854 adds that G_N must be regularized and flows with the regulator, the physical value being a fixed point. How dark matter itself gravitates is not addressed. My comparison: #11 §10's dictionary assigns the dual Einstein term an a⁻⁶ step in G_eff (flag 49, not derived) and maps dual curvature to negative dark radiation. In these papers the dual Einstein–Hilbert term gives a positive Λ.

answers.question: Q7
answers.answer: The nine papers give the dark sector no self-interaction, no dependence on relative velocity or on momentum overlap, no localization in x̃ or in momentum, and no condensate. What they do give is about metaparticles and dark-energy quanta. Metaparticle fields are bi-local φ(x, x̃) and non-commutative, with 'a non-trivial propagator and an IR sensitive dispersion relation' (2202.06890; Addazi §2.2.2.5; 2011.08852 §2). Non-locality allows infinite (Cuntz, quantum Boltzmann) statistics, applied to the quanta of dark energy, not of dark matter (2011.08852; 2202.05266; 2503.20854; Addazi §5.6). Non-commutativity also gives 'axion-like backgrounds' (2202.06890; Addazi). None of this resembles #11 §8's velocity gate or the momentum-localized monopoles of §12.

answers.question: Q8
answers.answer: Not addressed in these papers. None of the nine has magnetically charged, dyonic or topological objects. 'Monopole' and 'magnetic' have no hits in the dark-energy papers, apart from a Landau-level example in 2202.05266. Addazi's 'monopole' hits are gravitational mass monopoles in binaries, and 2312.00409's 'magnetic' hits are astrophysical fields.

answers.question: Q9
answers.answer: Nothing in the nine selects the polarization through a vacuum, a potential or an order parameter, and none calls the choice spontaneous or dynamical. 2503.20854 §1 says the non-commutativity makes 'the very notion of spacetime polarization observer dependent'. In 2202.06890 and Addazi §2.2.2.2, observer-dependent spacetimes are 'slices'/'sections' of quantum spacetime, depending on the probe, for example its momentum. 2212.00901 says 'A choice of basis is equivalent to a choice of polarization of phase space' and calls the Schrödinger polarization 'singular'. 2303.17495 says 'The change of polarization is a unitary change of basis', with modular spacetime 'corresponding to a generic polarization'. The polarization metric η is a dynamical field, but so are ω and H (2011.08852 §2; 2503.20854 App. B), whereas #11 P2′ keeps ω rigid. The 'Vacuum Selection' of the Snowmass title is selection among perturbative string vacua, compactifications that yield the Standard Model, by a mechanism modeled on horizontal gene transfer in biophysics. It is not the selection of a polarization. Whether the world with the other choice is equally lawful (#11 P5) is not discussed. This agrees with the record's literature check (§3, 'The vacuum'), which found no such mechanism.
evidence: 2202.05104, 'The vacuum selection principle in string theory'

answers.question: Q10
answers.answer:
In all of these papers dark energy is the geometry or curvature of the dual spacetime, to leading order a positive cosmological constant. Their predictions for w, the ratio of pressure to energy density (−1 for a cosmological constant), in order:

- **2202.05104, 2202.06890, Addazi et al.:** no w.
- **2011.08852:** no w stated. Its Λ(z)/Λ(0) = [1 − b(ξ)]/[1 − b(ξ₀)], ξ = ξ₀/(1+z), with Λ → 0 at early times. My computation: w(z = 0) = −2.0763, −1.3183 and −1.0255 for ξ₀ = 1, 5, 10, below −1 at every z computed.
- **2202.05266:** 'w_eff < −1' (abstract), with w_eff = −1 − ξ⁴e^{−ξ}/(18[1 − b(ξ)]), reaching −1 only as ξ₀ → ∞, 'corresponding to a cosmological constant'. 'This rules out quintessence models … with −1 < w_eff < −1/3'. Fits: H₀ = 68.9 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹ with ξ₀ = 18.4, and H₀ = 68.5 with ξ₀ = 14.8. My computation: w_eff(z = 0) = −1.0001 and −1.0010, and at z = 1, −1.0410 and −1.1087.
- **2503.20854, first model:** w(a) < −1 for all a; w₀ ≤ −1 and wₐ ≤ 0; (w₀, wₐ) → (−1, 0) as ξ₀ → ∞ and (−7/3, 0) as ξ₀ → 0. They call it 'clearly disfavored' by DESI DR2.
- **2503.20854, second model:** w(a) ≥ −1 'in all cases', wₐ < 0, w(0) = −1. It reproduces the DESI DR2 best fits (−0.42, −1.75), (−0.838, −0.62), (−0.667, −1.09) and (−0.752, −0.86) at the parameter points the paper lists; I checked each to within 0.01. Their conclusion: 'w(a) > −1'. My computation: the dark-energy density reaches zero at a future scale factor a = 1.59–2.26, where the cutoffs meet.
- **2212.00901, 2303.17495:** a small positive cosmological constant bounded by 1/ℓ²; no w.

**Against #11 §10 (τ, strictly w ≥ −1):** the 2022 letter and the 2025 first model predict the opposite sign of 1 + w, and the 2022 letter excludes quintessence outright. The 2025 second model shares #11 §13 row 4's signature (w ≥ −1, wₐ < 0, w → −1 at early times) and reaches DESI DR2's best fits. Those fits lie at wₐ/(1 + w₀) = −3.0 to −3.8, off #11's corridor wₐ ≈ −1.5(1 + w₀) (my computation). The mechanisms differ: dual curvature and infinite-statistics quanta between moving cutoffs, against hilltop quintessence on the Maslov circle.

**Against C5 (App. A item 9):** no paper describes a contracting or collapsing dual universe. The nearest elements are reciprocal scale relations. In 2011.08852 eqs. 17–19, Ẽ_UV E_IR = μ with E_IR = E₀/a. In 2503.20854 §2, δx δx̃ ∼ λ² converts our volume to a dual volume and a dual energy, and Λ changes with our scale factor because x and x̃ do not commute. #11 §10 maps 'dual stiff ↦ Λ' and 'dual curvature ↦ negative dark radiation'; in these papers the dual curvature itself is Λ.

answers.question: Q11
answers.answer: None of the nine is the earliest statement. The earliest of them to state the identification is 2011.08852 (17 November 2020), after Minic 2020 (29 February 2020) and Berglund–Hübsch–Minic (arXiv, October 2020). The Snowmass paper credits the idea to Minic 2020 and BHM 2021 ('has been recently proposed [29, 30]'). 2202.06890 and Addazi et al. credit Minic 2020 ([11], [408]). 2011.08852 cites the modified-dark-matter papers (2010–2020) for a dark-matter sector 'sensitive to dark energy'. No statement outside the school is cited. All nine predate the program's notebook (September 2026), so the four that state the identification are prior art for C1, each in a weaker form. For dark energy, they credit the dual-curvature origin to Berglund–Hübsch–Minic 2019 (arXiv:1905.08269, 1905.09463; also 1902.08617), and the Wien-spectrum dark energy goes back to Jejjala, Kavic and Minic 2007 (arXiv:0705.4581).
evidence: 2202.05104, 'Constraints on the nature of dark matter' and refs [29], [30]

answers.question: ω rigid or dynamical (#11 P2′)
answers.answer: The school's worldsheet action makes all three Born-geometry structures dynamical: 'The mutually compatible dynamical fields' ω_AB(X), η_AB(X), H_AB(X) (2011.08852 §2; 2503.20854 App. B, 'a (dynamical) Born geometry'). 2202.06890 describes the program of 'gravitization' as 'quantum mechanical structures that are traditionally fixed become dynamical'. #11 P2′ holds only ω rigid (the constancy of ℏ) and makes η emergent, crediting metastring theory only with η being dynamical. So the school goes further than P2′, making ω dynamical too. That is a difference to state where the two are compared, not a conflict with the record's attribution.

answers.question: Reciprocal observed and dual scales (a·ã = 1 analog)
answers.answer: The dark-energy papers pair an observed scale with a dual one reciprocally. In 2011.08852 eq. 17 and 2503.20854 eq. 16, Ẽ_UV E_IR = μ, so with E_IR = E₀/a the dual cutoff grows as Ẽ_UV = μa/E₀. 2503.20854 §3.4 uses E_IR Ẽ_IR = μ_IR and E_UV Ẽ_UV = μ_UV, from the metaparticle's p p̃ = μ. 2503.20854 §2 adds δx δx̃ ∼ λ² between our volume and the dual volume. 2212.00901 eq. 15 has LM/(2πℏ) = N^{1/4} at fixed N. My comparison: the first three are at the string scale and between cutoffs, and the papers call them assumptions ('as a first, naive, attempt, we simply assume'). #11 §10's a·ã = 1 instead follows from a rigid ω at ℏ. Only 2212.00901's relation is at ℏ, and the record's diameter note already cites it.

contradicts_record.record_says: "Their dual sector is correlated with ours by construction: … "Dark matter, dark energy and visible matter are naturally correlated in this description" (Berglund, Freidel et al. 2022). All three judges for C1 read this as predicting couplings between dark and visible matter beyond gravity" (notes/literature-check.md §3, 'What differs', the coupling); the same in wiki/method/literature-check.md ('The first conjecture': "Their dual sector is correlated with ours by construction.") and wiki/summary.md line 34 ("their sector correlated with ours")
contradicts_record.source_says: "(Dark matter, dark energy and visible matter are naturally correlated in this description [45, 46].)" (2202.06890, paragraph 'Observations'), where [45] is Ho, Minic, Ng, 'Cold Dark Matter with MOND Scaling', PLB 693 (2010) and [46] is Edmonds, Farrah, Minic, Ng, Takeuchi, 'Modified Dark Matter: Relating Dark Energy, Dark Matter and Baryonic Matter', IJMPD 27 (2017). The abstract of [46] (arXiv:1709.04388): "Such a critical acceleration is an effective phenomenological manifestation of MDM, and it is found in correlations between dark matter and baryonic matter in galaxy rotation curves." The Snowmass paper (2202.05104, 'Constraints on the nature of dark matter') likewise: "Various astrophysical observations point to intriguing correlations between dark matter, dark energy, and visible matter on the galactic, and galaxy cluster scales [8, 9]."
contradicts_record.why: This qualifies the record. As its references show, the quoted sentence refers to the observed MOND-like scaling of halos with baryons and Λ that the modified-dark-matter model fits, a correlation between distributions. The paper writes no interaction term and no coupling strength, and nothing that makes the correlation hold 'by construction'. In the Snowmass paper the correlations are observations the dual-SM picture is meant to explain ('we would like to understand whether…'). For these two sources, 'correlated by construction' and 'couplings beyond gravity' are the record's and the judges' readings, not the papers' words. The record's other sources for the coupling (Berglund–Hübsch–Minic 2023 Symmetry, Minic 2020, BHM 2021) are not among my papers, and this does not test them.

contradicts_record.record_says: "In the literature… Related [S]: … Hur et al. 2025, "In our model, dark energy stems from the curvature of the dual spacetime"; … None has a collapsing partner driving our present acceleration." (notes/literature-check.md §6, C5, 'Related')
contradicts_record.source_says: "The volume of spacetime x depends on a , and if we convert (via the “uncertainty” relation implied by the fundamental non-commutativity of x and \tilde{x} , \delta x\delta\tilde{x}\sim\lambda^{2} ) the volume of spacetime x to the volume of spacetime \tilde{x} , and this in turn, via the usual Heisenberg uncertainty relation to the energy in the dual spacetime \tilde{x} , we obtain the above equation" and "because the covariant spacetime labels x and \tilde{x} do not commute, they are not independent and thus, the change of the curvature in \tilde{x} , which is the origin of \Lambda , would, in principle, imply that \Lambda does change with the volume of x , of alternatively, with the scale factor a of the x spacetime, as well." (2503.20854 §2; both FOUND)
contradicts_record.why: The record's one-line summary understates the paper. Hur et al. tie the dual spacetime's size reciprocally to ours (δx δx̃ ∼ λ²) and make our Λ evolve with our scale factor because of it. In their second model the dual-energy band closes at a future a (1.59–2.26 at the DESI best fits, my computation), where the dark energy vanishes. 'None has a collapsing partner' still holds: the paper never says the dual space contracts or collapses, gives it no dynamics of its own ('only a motivation'), and works at the string scale λ² rather than ℏ. Still, this is the nearest published element in my papers to #11 §10's a·ã = 1 setting our dark energy, and it deserves a sentence where C5's related work is listed. The same paper also bears directly on #11 §13 row 4: its second model has w ≥ −1 and wₐ < 0 and reaches DESI DR2's best fits. The root CLAUDE.md records it only as a lead that 'bears on reading DESI's CPL quadrant against strict w ≥ −1'.

contradicts_record.record_says: "A review with 162 authors (Addazi et al. 2022) and Jejjala, Kavic, Minic and Takeuchi 2022 are partial too." (notes/literature-check.md §3, 'What is published'; its reference list resolves the second to "Dynamical dark energy and infinite statistics", Int. J. Mod. Phys. A 37, 2242001 (2022), arXiv:2011.08852)
contradicts_record.source_says: "arXiv:2011.08852v1 [hep-th] 17 Nov 2020" (2011.08852, HTML header; FOUND). arXiv API: 2011.08852 v1 2020-11-17, 2111.05659 v1 2021-11-10. The same four authors' paper actually posted in 2022, 2202.05266, says "We presuppose a consistent theory of quantum gravity such as string theory, but we are largely agnostic about its details." (§1; FOUND) and has no dark-matter statement.
contradicts_record.why: A minor dating point. The year labels are journal years: 'Jejjala, Kavic, Minic and Takeuchi 2022' was first posted on 17 November 2020, and 'Addazi et al. 2022' on 10 November 2021. The JKMT label is easily confused with the same authors' 2022 paper (arXiv:2202.05266), which does not state the identification and predicts w < −1. No verdict changes, since all are before September 2026. A wiki page that dates and links these papers should use the arXiv v1 dates.
